title: B004 Appendix J: Good practice example of poetry – line indicator method

illustrates.quote: Poetry may be written continuously with the line indicator placed at the end of each verse line. Each stanza begins in cell 3 of a new line. The line indicator occurs at the end of each stanza except the last. It doesn’t appear at the end of a poem or verse extract.

blocks.features: The same two stanzas of Edward Lear's "The Owl and the Pussy-Cat" as the line-by-line example, but no separate print rendering is given here in B004.txt beyond a repeat reference to the same lines already quoted for the line-by-line method (the guiding text introduces this second method as an alternative way of BRAILLING the identical print poem, not a new print excerpt).

lines.text: The Owl and the Pussycat went to sea
They took some honey, and plenty of money,
Wrapped up in a five pound note.
The Owl looked up to the stars above
And sang to a small guitar,
“O lovely Pussy! O Pussy, my love,
What a beautiful Pussy you are,
What a beautiful Pussy you are!”

print.notes: No new print text is given for this second example in B004.txt; it reuses the identical Owl-and-Pussycat print poem already given for the line-by-line method, now transcribed with the alternative line-indicator technique.
print.surroundingText: Follows the rule text describing the 'line indicator' method for transcribing poetry, offered as a space-saving alternative to the 'line by line' method.
print.printFeatures: Same print poem as b004-j-1; no separate print image for this second example.
